items.q: What should you remember about **Preparation = luck**?
items.a: **define luck as preparation** meeting opportunity; shortlisted people prepared, they didn't get lucky.

items.q: What should you remember about **Top 10 questions are predictable**?
items.a: **yet most candidates don't** prepare answers (see top 10 interview questions).

items.q: What should you remember about **"Tell us about yourself" is always first**?
items.a: **winging it fails on** the question everyone knows is coming.

items.q: What should you remember about **Adjectives fail**?
items.a: **"integrity, honesty, punctuality" and** "my weakness is perfectionism" don't connect; stories do.

items.q: What should you remember about **Origin story format**?
items.a: **2–3 minutes; childhood or formative** memory; show character; bridge to why you're right for *this* job.

items.q: What should you remember about **Link story to role**?
items.a: **the eBay/early-adopter thread maps** directly to "Head of Innovation" requirements.

items.q: What should you remember about **Make it conversational**?
items.a: **ask the interviewer questions** mid-story; humor and rapport beat Q&A stiffness.

items.q: What should you remember about **Neurochemistry shift**?
items.a: **storytelling releases dopamine, endorphins,** oxytocin; interviewers relax and engage as peers.
**stories separate you from** hundreds of applicants who only list traits.
